theme: Ephesus, disciples receive the Spirit; the riot
readingInstruction: Read Acts 19:1-41. Paul spends nearly three years in Ephesus. Disciples of John receive the Spirit, extraordinary miracles occur, magic books are burned, and a riot breaks out over the goddess Artemis. Notice the power of the word.
settingTheScene: Ephesus was the leading city of Asia Minor, home of the great temple of Artemis (Diana), one of the seven wonders of the ancient world. It was a center of magic and trade. Paul based his ministry here for about three years (AD 52 to 55), and the Ephesian church became one of the most important in the early church. From here, all of Asia heard the word of the Lord.
observation: “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” (19:2).
“And when Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied” (19:6).
“He withdrew from them and took the disciples with him, reasoning daily in the hall of Tyrannus” (19:9).
“Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?” (19:15).
“And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all” (19:19).
“So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily” (19:20).
“Saying that gods made with hands are not gods” (19:26).
interpretation:
Paul finds some disciples in Ephesus who knew only the baptism of John. When he asks, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” they have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit. Paul explains that John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance, pointing to the one who would come after him, Jesus. They are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul lays his hands on them, the Spirit comes. These were Old Testament believers who were brought into the new covenant era, a unique transitional moment, and not a pattern for later believers, since every Christian receives the Spirit at conversion (Romans 8:9).

Paul speaks boldly in the synagogue for three months, then moves to the hall of Tyrannus, where he reasons daily for two years, “so that all the residents of Asia heard the word of the Lord.” God does extraordinary miracles by the hands of Paul. Some Jewish exorcists try to use the name of Jesus as a formula, and the evil spirit answers, “Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?” The man overpowers them. The name of Jesus is not a magic word. It is a person, and only those who know him have authority in his name. The event brings fear, and the name of Jesus is extolled.

Many believers come, confessing and divulging their practices. A number of those who had practiced magic burn their books, valued at fifty thousand pieces of silver. “So the word of the Lord continued to increase and prevail mightily.” This is the evidence of real conversion: they gave up what was dear and profitable.

Then comes a riot. Demetrius, a silversmith, whose shrine-making trade is threatened, stirs up the craftsmen: “Not only in Ephesus but in almost all of Asia this Paul has persuaded and turned away a great many people, saying that gods made with hands are not gods.” The whole city is filled with confusion, and for two hours they shout, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!” The town clerk calms the crowd, pointing out that the Christians have neither robbed temples nor blasphemed their goddess, and that if Demetrius has a complaint, there are courts. He dismisses the assembly. Notice how Luke shows that the gospel is not a threat to public order, though it is a threat to idolatry and the economies that depend on it.
connection: Matthew 3:11 records John’s promise of baptism with the Holy Spirit. Ephesians 1:13-14 says believers are sealed with the Spirit. The letter to the Ephesians and Revelation 2:1-7 address the same church. Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids sorcery. Psalm 115:4-8 mocks idols made by hands. 1 Corinthians 15:32 and 16:8-9 mention Paul’s time in Ephesus. 2 Timothy 1:15-18 mentions Onesiphorus. 1 John 5:21 says to keep yourselves from idols.
application:
Is there a “book” you need to burn, something from your old life that holds you?

Ask whether you know Jesus personally or just use his name.

Ask where the economics of idolatry affect your life, such as consumerism and entertainment.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to help you know Jesus rather than just use his name.
Thank him for the Holy Spirit.
Ask him to expose any idols in your life.
